Nyirmartonfalva Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Óvoda utca 6, Hungary

Demolished. Nyírmártonfalva's cemetery was established as early as 1870, per that year's cadastral map, and demolished in 1970 to build a primary school on the site. The Jewish population fluctuated between 7 people in 1840 and a peak of 54 by 1930, settling at 46 by 1941; in 1942, young Jewish adults were taken for forced labor. By 1944, eight Jewish families remained; following Passover that year, they were sent to the Simapuszta Ghetto and deported to Auschwitz on May 22 — none returned. In 2019, the municipality voted to place a commemorative plaque in cooperation with descendants of Nyírmártonfalva's Jews.
